evidence: Wikipedia's article on Tony Allen: Blur's 'Music Is My Radar' (2000) referred to him; Allen heard it and contacted Damon Albarn, and the two formed The Good, the Bad & the Queen, whose debut came out in 2007. Albarn later called Allen his number one musical teacher.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: 'Music Is My Radar' is a British band trying to play an Afrobeat groove: a dry, busy drum part, a short repeating bass figure, and Albarn singing a line about Tony Allen getting him dancing. Put it next to Allen's own playing and you can hear both the admiration and the distance. Then listen to The Good, the Bad & the Queen (2007), where Allen himself plays the drums.

explanation: In 2000 Blur released 'Music Is My Radar', a song that mentions Tony Allen. Allen heard it and got in touch with Damon Albarn, and they started making music together. Albarn later called Allen his most important musical teacher. It is a rare case of a later musician's tribute reaching the earlier one and starting a collaboration, and it carries Afrobeat into Britpop through a named person rather than a vague 'world music' influence.
